why: Authoring the first Area 1 sections put four independent readers on the official CMR text with instructions to follow the source over a rule summary and report any divergence. None found a rule summary that CONTRADICTS its authority. Several found summaries that UNDER-SPECIFY the authority they themselves cite, which is the defect class that has driven repair rounds: a section can only teach what a rule carries, so a thin summary silently caps what the guide can say.

classes.under_specified_rule_summary: The rule cites an authority whose content it does not carry.
classes.uncovered_provision: Official text with real examination value that no canonical rule carries at all.
classes.official_text_oddity: An inconsistency inside the official source itself; nothing to fix, worth knowing.
classes.contradicts_authority: The rule asserts something its own cited authority does not support. The most serious class.
classes.wrong_pinpoint: The rule's cited provision is not the one that governs the actor the guide teaches, even where the substance matches.
classes.boilerplate_rule_record: The rule carries template filler in exceptions/common_confusions and an empty numeric_facts where its authority is full of numbers and carve-outs. A v1 skeleton never finished.
classes.misleading_guidance_field: The rule's own exceptions or common_confusions field teaches something the authority does not support. Worse than a thin summary, because the field exists to correct misreadings and instead creates one.
classes.over_reads_authority: The rule states a threshold, qualifier or limit the authority does not contain, narrowing or widening the duty.
classes.wrong_actor: The rule names the wrong duty-holder. Distinct because actor_and_scope is its own audit criterion and a wrong actor changes who is answerable.
classes.cross_board_conflict: The Pharmacy Board and Medicine Board regulations state the same rule differently. Neither record is wrong; the sources diverge.
classes.broken_authority_url: The rule's authority URL does not resolve. The validator checks that a url field is present, not that it points anywhere.

findings.detail: One generic sentence against four distinct 14-day duties: online licensing profile contact details; name change with sworn statement, photo ID copy and any further Board documentation; ANY ARREST, pending criminal charge or conviction, the duty attaching at arrest; and disciplinary action as defined in 247 CMR 2.00 or loss of certification.
Skips 4.02(2), the late-renewal route on payment of an annual fee, applicable back fees and a late fee. It is what makes the 'I paid this morning, may I work?' question answerable.
Omits 3.02(1)(d), reciprocity fees non-refundable once reviewed and acted upon, and 3.02(3)(a)1, the Board must receive an official FPGEC certificate copy from NABP on the non-approved-school branch.

Says a covered registrant completes 'additional' annual compounding hours. The official text allocates subject matter inside the 20-hour annual minimum rather than adding to it, and the released bank treats the law hours as counting within the 20.

Compresses the evaluation duty to 'evaluate the program'. The text is 'faculty, learning experiences, instructional methods, facilities and educational resources'. A released question is keyed to the fuller version.
Renders a proof provision as a quantity provision. 4.03(3) is a statement submitted with the renewal application under the penalties of perjury; the summary drops the mechanism.
Omits the qualifier 'except where otherwise prohibited by federal or state laws and regulations'.
Omits the required training-program topic list, so no section can teach what an approved programme must cover.
Pharmacy intern licence eligibility. Who may become an intern at all is untaught while supervision and hours are taught.
Internship hours may be acquired throughout a calendar year. A released question's distractor turns on it.
Intern licence application contents.
CE provider application contents including the eight permitted subject areas, academic courses, education methods and faculty competence documentation.
Closed by MA-RX-FORMAT-CONTENT in this session; listed so the class is visible.
Heading says ACPE-accredited AND Board-approved; operative 3.01(1)(b) says OR.
Identical sentence reads 'may register with NABP to take MPJE' in one branch and 'must' in the other.
Cross-references 247 CMR 4.11, which does not exist; the chapter runs 4.01 to 4.08.
Says 'registered pharmacy preceptor' where 8.01(3) and 8.01(16) say 'pharmacist preceptor'.

Conflates two paragraphs. (a) covers a lost UNFILLED form and binds only the purchaser; (b) covers theft or loss of used or unused forms and expressly excludes losses 'other than in the course of transmission', so a form lost in the mail owes no (b) report. The summary also names the local DEA Diversion Field Office where the regulation says the Special Agent in Charge in the Divisional Office.

Drops the word that is the whole test: records must be readily retrievable SEPARATELY FROM all other records, not merely 'from' them. Also compresses the separate-maintenance duty and the two-year inspection-availability duty into one.

Omits 'endorsed' from the defect list, renders (a)(2) narrower than 'any alteration, erasure, or change of any description', and omits the supplier's duty to return the original with a statement of reason and the purchaser's retention duty.
Enumerates the transfer submissions but omits the description of the date and procedure for transferring controlled substances.
Says a resident pharmacy must give notice; the regulation binds 'a Massachusetts pharmacy AND a Manager of Record'. MA-PHARMACY-CLOSURE-CS understates 6.13(6) the same way.
Compresses the particulars to 'the named particulars of both pharmacies', omitting (g) the transfer date and (h) the security procedures.

Cites 10.06(1) through (5); the section actually runs (1) through (9), so consent agreements, out-of-state discipline, summary cease and desist and summary quarantine are invisible from the rule. Also compresses 10.06(5), losing that suspension or revocation is reached either by adjudicated decision OR by executing a consent agreement.

Attributes the 15-business-day clock to 10.08(1) notices alone when the text reaches 10.06(8) and (9) too; omits 10.08(2) on how long a notice stands; and calls the notice non-disciplinary where the regulation applies that word to what the notice imposes.

Numbers correct, three qualifiers missing: 'in a manner and format determined by the Board', the cross-reference to 247 CMR 10.06, and that a pending charge or conviction is 'as defined in 247 CMR 10.02'.

'Revoked' appears in BOTH tiers: (6) covers revocation or suspension of six months to two years, (7) covers revocation or suspension of more than two years. Nothing distinguishes which tier a revocation falls in, and a suspension under six months falls in neither.

Directs disposal 'in accordance with federal regulations at 21 CFR 1307.21', a pinpoint that no longer exists. Registrant disposal now sits in 21 CFR part 1317, with 1317.05 covering registrant disposal.

Non-resident pharmacy must apply to change its designated pharmacist in charge within 90 days of the predecessor's removal or resignation. The contrast with the resident Manager of Record change under 6.10, which states no day count, is the exam-useful point and nothing carries it.
Separate ten-element eligibility test for a proposed Manager of Record, distinct from the 6.03 owner elements and including grounds 6.03 does not carry.

Who may obtain and execute Form 222, power of attorney, one item per line and one supplier per form, endorsement to a second supplier, return of unused forms on registration termination, and cancellation. Partly owned by FED-FORM222-POA and FED-FORM222-CANCEL, which sit in area 3 rather than with the ordering material.

Asserts that under 247 CMR 8.05 a pharmacy INTERN may handle Schedule II controlled substances under direct pharmacist supervision. The official text carries no such general grant: 8.05(1) is the pharmacist-accountability sentence, 8.05(2)(a)-(b) name only the pharmacy technician and the certified pharmacy technician, and the sole operative intern permission is 8.05(3), confined to hydrocodone-only extended release medication not in an abuse deterrent form. The rule appears to have generalised that narrow carve-out into a broad authority. MA-CII-SUPPORT-HANDLING states the same territory correctly.
findings.blocked_by: MA-Q-0076 (RELEASED) snapshots this rule, so it cannot be corrected in place without unpublishing that question.
findings.mitigation: MA-Q-0076 turns on the 8.05(1)-(2) grade split and does not rest on the intern claim, so nothing currently relies on the erroneous part. SG-MA-SUPPORT-PERSONNEL follows the official text and teaches the intern row as limited to the 8.05(3) product.

findings.detail: Carries only the first sentence. The provision continues: if the Manager of Record is unexpectedly not available, another registered pharmacist shall perform the controlled substances inventory. Without it the rule cannot answer the unplanned-absence branch, where a pre-absence inventory is by definition impossible.

Omits the object the official text supplies -- disciplinary action 'against an individual or entity licensed or registered by the Board' -- which is the load-bearing clause for reach, since it puts entity credentials on the same footing as individual ones.
Says 'registered' where the text says 'registered or licensed'.
Says conclusive evidence 'in any disciplinary proceeding based upon the conviction'; the text reads 'in any disciplinary proceeding AGAINST SUCH PERSON based upon the conviction'.

The Manager of Record's duties toward support personnel: planning and maintaining staffing that promotes patient safety, enforcing staffing policies, maintaining the records 247 CMR 8.02(6) requires, and ensuring the technician training programme is Board-approved and current. Squarely inside a section's declared scope with no rule to carry it.
Conviction, guilty plea, nolo contendere or admission to sufficient facts as a listed disciplinary ground. It is what gives the 10.02 conviction definition its operative bite, and no rule cites it.
The intern tag asks for the intern's NAME; the three technician provisions each confine the tag to the individual's FIRST name.

8.05(2) grants Schedule II transporting to the technician and transporting-and-handling to the certified technician, and does not name the TRAINEE; 8.03(4)(b) lets a trainee perform the duties of a pharmacy technician under direct supervision. Whether that derivatively reaches 8.05(2)(a) is unresolved by either provision, and 8.05(3) does name the trainee, so the section addresses that tier where it means to.

1301.74 is titled 'Other security controls for NON-PRACTITIONERS'. A pharmacy is a practitioner -- 1301.75 speaks of 'pharmacies and institutional practitioners', and 1317.05(c)(2)(iv) says 'practitioners (i.e., retail pharmacies and hospitals/clinics)'. The provision that reaches a pharmacy is 21 CFR 1301.76(b). The substance is the same (written notice in one business day, DEA Form 106, the same six significance factors), but the wording differs: 1301.74(c) says '45 calendar days' and 1301.76(b) says '45 days'. The section was written on the rule's own pinpoint so it is accurate either way, but the authority needs correcting.

Three errors in one sentence. Says 'Schedule II' where the text says 'Schedules I or II'; says 'more than 1,000 units' where the text says 'more than 1,000 tablets or capsules', a gap that decides liquids; and omits that the exact-or-estimate choice is confined to an OPENED commercial container, so the summary reads as a general Schedule II counting rule when the regulation is a rule about opened containers sitting on top of container-level entries. The pinpoint (e)(6) is correct in the current CFR; an older codification put it at (e)(3).

Renders the exception clause as 'unless another provision requires longer'. The text reads 'Except as provided in paragraphs (a)(1) and (2)', which are LOCATION carve-outs for central recordkeeping, not duration ones. Also drops 'and copying' and drops that the two years run 'from the date of such inventory or record'.
Omits the operative half: delivery confined to the registered location, no re-routing after despatch, receipt by an employee in person, and destruction within 30 calendar days.

Lists 'substance, method, place, date, and witness information' as though the regulation requires them. 1304.21(e) requires a complete and accurate record and the names and signatures of two witnessing employees; the remaining items are fields of the DEA Form 41 itself, and 1317.95 does not mention Form 41 at all.

findings.rule_id: MA-CS-SECURITY, FED-THEFT-LOSS-DEA, FED-DISPOSAL-NONRETRIEVABLE, FED-FORM41, FED-REVERSE-DISTRIBUTOR, FED-INVENTORY-COUNT, FED-CS-RECORDS-2Y
findings.detail: Seven rules carry template filler in exceptions and common_confusions and an empty numeric_facts, while their authorities are full of numbers and carve-outs: 247 CMR 9.21's 14-day and 2-year camera retention and 10-day Schedule II perpetual reconciliation, 1301.74(c)'s one business day and 45 calendar days, 1317.15(d)'s 30 calendar days, 9.21(11) and (12)'s two real exclusions, 1304.21(e)'s Form 41 exception, and 1317.05(a)(5)'s standing approval.

A registrant shall report theft, loss or suspected tampering of any controlled substance to the Commissioner's designated agent WITHIN 24 HOURS of discovery, submitting a copy of the Department's Drug Intake Form. This is the highest-value Massachusetts-versus-federal contrast in the area -- 24 hours and a Drug Intake Form against one business day and a Form 106 -- and no canonical rule carries it. MA-CS-PERSONNEL-SCREENING's authority stops at 700.005(B). 700.005(A) physical security and (C) security of mail are uncovered for the same reason.

The federal pharmacy storage norm, dispersing Schedules II-V throughout the stock of NONCONTROLLED substances. Without it the direct contrast with 247 CMR 9.21(2)'s dispersal through SCHEDULE VI stock cannot be taught.

General inventory requirements: a complete and accurate record of all controlled substances on hand, kept at the registered location, a SEPARATE inventory for each registered location, and taken as of opening or close of business with which one indicated. The three inventory rules cite only (b), (c) and (e)(6).

The pharmacy filing regime -- Schedule I and II records separate from all others, III-V separate or readily retrievable -- and the rule that executed order forms and inventories are kept at each registered location rather than centrally.

No perpetual inventory is required federally; Massachusetts registration renewal deadlines; and the three-year federal DEA registration term. The last makes the classic biennial-inventory-versus-three-year-registration contrast unavailable.

A SECOND Massachusetts theft-or-loss route. Drug Store, sterile compounding, complex non-sterile compounding and nuclear pharmacies located in Massachusetts report theft or loss of a significant amount of controlled substances TO THE BOARD, submitting a copy of 'Report of Theft or Loss of Controlled Substance' AND DEA Form 106, WITHIN SEVEN DAYS. Taken with 105 CMR 700.005(D)'s 24-hour Drug Control Program report and the federal one-business-day Form 106 route, one event carries three separate reports on three clocks to three recipients -- and only the federal one has a canonical rule. MA-LICENSEE-CHANGE-14D nominally cites 247 CMR 20.03 whole but is an area 1 licensee-change rule, which is also why the coverage gate did not fire.

CQI records: a written programme description on the premises readily available to all personnel, and QRE records kept a minimum of TWO YEARS from the date of the QRE report, filed by date, storable off site. No rule cites 15.04. The two-year QRE retention is the natural counterpart to the five-year serious-event retention, and the 'what record survives' column is materially poorer without it.

20.02's reporting requirements do not reach non-resident pharmacies, and a non-resident pharmacy reports improper dispensing into Massachusetts causing serious injury or death within seven business days of discovering the improper dispensing -- a different trigger from 20.02(1). Neither is carried.

Implies a single Board recipient; 20.02(2) names three -- the Board, the FDA MedWatch Program, and the Betsy Lehman Center for Patient Safety and Medical Error Reduction. Also drops the product-origin narrowing to drugs manufactured, produced or compounded at the pharmacy, blurs two distinct clock triggers into one, and is silent on 20.02(3) despite citing it.

Says 'must maintain' where the text says 'shall establish', and omits all six minimum provisions (a)-(f), including 15.02(1)(a)'s duty to designate an individual responsible for monitoring compliance.

Omits the duty to train all pharmacy personnel to escalate any quality related event to the pharmacist immediately on discovery, and omits 'other members of the healthcare team' from the recipients of the pharmacist's response.
Carries only (2)(a) and is silent on the four mandatory content elements in (2)(b), which its own citation covers.

Omits (3)(a)3's indicators measured over a designated period and the whole of (3)(b), the duty to inform pharmacy personnel of resulting changes. Its 'use the findings to improve systems' clause reads closer to 15.02(1)(e) than to the cited 15.03(3).

As promulgated 247 CMR 15.00 is 15.02 to 15.04 only, with no 15.01, and contains NO confidentiality, privilege or discovery-protection provision. No rule carries one either. A section on quality events cannot teach the confidential-versus-discoverable question at all; the section states that these rules confer no such protection rather than inferring one.

Drops 'justified by a documented medical need as determined by the prescribing practitioner', leaving a bare prescriber determination looking sufficient. It also mis-frames the provision: s. 39D is an EXCLUSION -- compounding shall not include preparing commercially available FDA-approved drugs -- which the patient-specific limb lifts, rather than a permission. The statutory illustrations (removal of a dye for medical reasons, change in strength, change in dosage form or delivery mechanism) are also dropped.

Conflates two different addressee lists. 6.15(2) reaches sterile, non-resident sterile and institutional sterile pharmacies; 6.15(4) reaches those three plus COMPLEX NON-STERILE. The summary carries the (2) list into (4). It also omits that 6.15(2)'s application is one to remodel or to change configuration or square footage, not a standalone engineering-control application.

Both carry the proposition that a licence is required, but cite only the APPLICATION sections 6.06 and 6.07. The licence requirement lives in 6.02(2) and (3), which is also more specific: sterile needs a Drug Store licence AND a sterile licence, or an institutional sterile licence; complex non-sterile needs a Drug Store licence AND a complex non-sterile licence, with no institutional alternative.

Says 'each applicable USP chapter'. The text reads 'each chapter of the United States Pharmacopeia', qualified by 'unless otherwise regulated by the Board' -- a broader incorporation than 'applicable' suggests.

The only USP-specific rules are marked UNCLEAR or HOLD and are therefore not canonical, so no section can define a secondary engineering control or say what an ISO classification signifies. The word 'hazardous' appears ZERO times in both 247 CMR 6.00 and 247 CMR 9.00: every hazardous-drug obligation in this corpus is derivative of 9.01(3)'s USP incorporation.
Institutional sterile compounding licensure and non-resident licensure carry no canonical rule, though 6.08 is named as an addressee of 6.15(2) and (4).
Speaks only of 'an application to change the configuration or square footage of a pharmacy', omitting 'to remodel' which (1), (2) and (4) all carry.

Its common_confusions says 'Extending the offer duty to refills, when the statutory trigger is a new prescription.' True of the statute, but 247 CMR 9.18(1)'s offer trigger is wider -- each person who RECEIVES A PRESCRIPTION MEDICATION, not limited to new prescriptions. Read alone the note teaches that no offer is owed on a refill. The two triggers coexist.
Requires 'a meaningful offer or provision'. The phrase MEANINGFUL OFFER appears nowhere in 247 CMR 9.18 or M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 21A. It is a formula the rule record introduced.

Says the pharmacist must 'resolve clinically significant issues'. CLINICALLY SIGNIFICANT appears nowhere in 9.17; 9.17(2) is triggered 'upon identifying ANY OF THE ABOVE', with no significance threshold, so the rule invites a candidate to filter where the regulation does not. Its trigger also drops 'or medication order' and 'or delivered to a patient or a patient's agent'. And it carries none of the ten identification items in 9.17(1)(a)-(j) although it is the ONLY record carrying 9.17(1) at all.
Drops 'potential drug therapy problems due to' from the screening clause, making the listed items the direct objects of screening rather than the causes of the problems screened for.

Compresses the profile identifiers to 'the patient's identifying details'. The text is name, address, CONTACT INFORMATION, date of birth or age, and gender. Note the regulation says contact information where s. 21A says telephone number.
Generalises the exception to 'applicable federal regulations'. The statute names regulations of the Federal Health Care Financing Administration under 42 USC 1396r-8.

'Nothing in this section shall be construed to require a pharmacist to provide counseling if the person presenting the prescription declines to accept such offer for counseling.' Arguably the most testable sentence in the statute and no rule carries it. A section can teach that a refusal is recordable and that its absence raises a presumption, but not the discharge itself.

The statutory counselling content list (1)-(8), which is NOT identical to 247 CMR 9.18(5): the statute's (6) is proper storage with no disposal, its (8) is missed dose with no adverse reaction, and its (4) adds 'including their avoidance and the action required if they occur'. Only the CMR list is carried, so a question keyed to the statutory list is unanswerable from the bank.

Two-year readily-retrievable prescription records, Schedule II / III-V / VI segregation, printable electronic prescriptions and stored images. No canonical rule carries any of it -- MA-PATIENT-PROFILE-DUTY is the only record citing 9.16 and pinpoints only (7) and (8). Also means no rule says where the 9.17(2) drug-review record lives or how long it is kept.

Says the pamphlet is required when A PHARMACY dispenses. The statute reads 'A PHARMACIST shall distribute the pamphlet when dispensing a narcotic or controlled substance contained in schedule II or III.' The rule also omits, inside its own cited authority, that the department distributes the pamphlet to pharmacies NOT INCLUDING INSTITUTIONAL PHARMACIES, and that s. 21 enumerates nine required pamphlet topics.

Framed as a controlled-substance label rule. Section 21's fourth paragraph applies the labeling provisions to 'the compounding and dispensing of drugs on the oral, electronic or written prescription of a licensed and registered prescriber under section 9', so the element list is not confined to controlled substances. Its exceptions entry is also looser than the statute: the only carve-out inside the element list is that the PATIENT'S NAME is required unless it is a veterinary prescription, not a whole-label exemption, and 'any specific statutory labeling exception' names nothing.

A pharmacy shall utilise a computerized pharmacy system for processing prescriptions and maintaining patient profiles. NO canonical rule cites it. It is the premise that makes 9.04(3)'s computer-printed label and 9.04(7)'s product-identity recording coherent, so this is a hole in the rule bank rather than merely outside one section's scope.

'A pharmacy intern, or certified pharmacy technician who has the approval of the pharmacist on duty may receive new prescriptions over the telephone.' The relative clause is grammatically capable of attaching to both limbs or to the technician limb alone. The natural reading, and the only one giving the clause independent work, attaches it to the technician; MA-RX-TELEPHONE-RECEIPT and MA-Q-0376's key both take that reading.

The institutional sterile compounding carve-out lists 9.04(4), (5), (6), (9), (10), (12), (13) and (14) -- conspicuously NOT (3), (7) or (8), so the label-printing, product-identity and related duties are not carved out. An examinable asymmetry.

'Required Agreement Terms for All Practice Settings' -- the enumerated mandatory contents of EVERY collaborative practice agreement: disease states as primary or co-morbid, specific prescribing authority, detailed practice protocols, risk-management description, documentation of initiation/modification/discontinuation, outcome measurements, informed-consent procedures, forwarding procedures and periods with urgent-communication and unavailability procedures, and two attestations. NO rule in data/rules cites 16.04(2). This is the substance of what a CDTM agreement must contain and the guide cannot teach any of it. 247 CMR 16.04(1) is likewise uncarried.

The Pharmacy Board says the agreement must specify when and how AN AUTHORIZED PHARMACIST may delegate; the Medicine Board says A SUPERVISING PHYSICIAN. MA-CDTM-DELEGATION-TERMS follows its own cited authority correctly; the divergence is in the sources.

Conditions electronic transmission on four instruments -- M.G.L. c. 94C s. 23(g), 105 CMR 721.00, AND 247 CMR 9.01(19) and 9.07(1)(a). The summary lists only the first two, and omits that the definition is expressly bounded to 243 CMR 2.12.

Its numeric_facts conditions read 'at least; on a biennial basis', but the cited statutory definition says only 'subject to review and renewal on a biennial basis'. The 'at least every two years' formulation, and the identification of who must review, come from 247 CMR 16.04(4), which the record does not cite.
The qualifier 'in accordance with the terms of the CDTM agreement' attaches to BOTH sentences in the official text; the summary attaches it only to the continuity duty.

Cites 243 CMR 2.12 at section level rather than the operative paragraph, and drops its third sentence: the supervising physician must maintain the patient's medical record in his or her custody and make it available on request during a Board of Registration in Medicine investigation.
The pharmacy-board provision omits the CEU alternative that both M.G.L. c. 112 s. 24B1/2(b)(5) and 243 CMR 2.12(2)(e) carry: 'five additional contact hours OR 0.5 continuing education units'.

Both point at .../Chapter112/Section24B1~2, which returns 404. The five other statute rules in the cluster use .../Section24B%201~2 -- the difference is a dropped space before '1~2'. MA-CDTM-QUALIFICATIONS also puts the rule title in authority[0].name where the other records put 'Massachusetts General Laws'.

Compresses six statutory requirements into five noun phrases and DROPS the sixth entirely (application to participate in the MassHealth programme should chapter 118E regulations be promulgated). All three numbers vanish -- $1,000,000 liability coverage, five years of experience, five contact hours or 0.5 CEU -- and numeric_facts is empty.

Drops the third sentence of (3)(d): the Board may revoke a physician's right to participate for any of the grounds in 243 CMR 1.03(5). Its notice clause also flattens (3)(e)'s three specific triggers -- a Voluntary Agreement Not to Practice, a summary suspension, or an approved final decision and order or consent agreement -- into a general 'where the Board acts'. That hides an exam-decisive fact: a controlled-substances registration action is NOT one of the triggers, so no notification duty arises from that event alone.

Drops 'with a patient' from the statute's clause and writes 'collaborative drug therapy management' where the text says 'collaborative drug therapy'. It also cites two authorities that use different labels for the same norm -- the statute says RETAIL pharmacy, 247 CMR 16.04(7)(b)-(c) says COMMUNITY pharmacy -- without noting the equivalence.
Drops the proviso 'provided the following requirements are met', which is what turns (G)(1)-(G)(10) into conditions on the power rather than neighbouring facts.

Cites s. 20 without disclosing that it is titled 'Oral prescriptions' and governs oral transmission, which is what makes (G)(7)'s particulars a list of things told to the dispensing pharmacist rather than printed on a form.

(G)(10) is the consequential one: a copy of an initial prescription, modification or discontinuation goes to the supervising physician WITHIN 24 HOURS of issuance unless more urgent notification is required. It is general to all CDTM prescribing, yet the only 24-hour rule in the bank rests on M.G.L. c. 112 s. 24B1/2(c)(5) and is retail-limited. (G)(9), the record of controlled substances held for immediate treatment, is likewise uncovered.

The regulation's own pharmacist qualifications, which NARROW the statute (the PharmD route requires an agreement entered on or before 30 June 2017, and 16.02(1)(a) adds 'unrestricted and in good standing'); the supervising physician's POSITIVE qualifications, where the bank carries only the disqualifying half; and the 243 CMR definitions of Authorized Pharmacist, Community Pharmacy and a heavier Patient definition requiring written consent in a community pharmacy.
Limits a retail-setting pharmacist to Schedule VI 'in accordance with 105 CMR 700.003(G)(3)', but (G)(3) is the general-compliance limb, not a schedule provision.

how_to_use: An under-specified summary is corrected by enriching the rule, which is only safe where no RELEASED question's final adjudication snapshots it. Check that first; where it is snapshotted the correction waits for a question-lane cycle. An uncovered provision needs a new additive rule, which has no blast radius.

question_lane_referrals.issue: Rests only on FED-FORM222-LOSS. Its facts are a Form 222 mailed to a supplier that never arrived, and its keyed answer ends with making the applicable DEA loss report. 21 CFR 1305.16(b) excludes losses in the course of transmission, so on these facts no such report is owed. Left unmapped by SG-CS-ORDERING rather than absorbed, so the guide need not agree with the key.

A distractor is refuted by 247 CMR 8.01(5), which no canonical rule carries. The question remains answerable from the section's own material, but the elimination the explanation relies on is not reachable.
question_lane_referrals.action: Either add a rule for 8.01(5) or revise the explanation.

question_lane_referrals.issue: Tagged area 3 while its sole rule MA-PRODUR is area 2. A blueprint-area tagging inconsistency, not a legal error.
